primitives.name: Early Acceleration
primitives.verbatim_quote: We define early acceleration over the first second of movement, later acceleration over 10–20 yards, and retention as the speed ratio near 40 versus 20 yards.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Post-onset motion only; excludes reaction time.

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives encode distinct aspects of sprint dynamics—early acceleration, late acceleration, and speed retention—each defined over specific temporal or spatial domains. Early acceleration is derived from instantaneous velocity gain in the first second post-onset, excluding reaction time. Late acceleration is computed over a fixed spatial range (10–20 yd), capturing mid-sprint behavior. Retention is a ratio of velocities at two points, measuring top-end speed sustainability. These operators are not mutually exclusive but form a basis for evaluating speed-building strategies. Their failure modes include measurement noise, insufficient data coverage, and misalignment with actual game scenarios. Nested audits reveal that early acceleration is not selected in pooled analyses, suggesting it lacks strong predictive value for draft outcomes. However, post-screen analysis shows a discovery effect, indicating potential utility when properly validated. The lack of transferability under fixed windows implies that context matters, which GSE models via Bayesian state transitions. GSI’s conformal inference addresses selection bias by validating against out-of-fold data, while GSE ensures robustness through repeated sampling and sensitivity analysis.
